question:
(a) Explain why total internal reflection cannot occur when light travels from air to glass.
(b) A ray travels from glass to air. If the refractive index of glass is $1.6$, find the critical angle for the glass-air interface.

options.A:
(a) Total internal reflection requires travel from denser to rarer medium. Air to glass is rarer to denser, so refraction is possible at all incidence angles and TIR cannot occur.
(b) For glass-air, $\sin i_c=\dfrac{1}{n}=\dfrac{1}{1.6}=0.625$, so $i_c=\sin^{-1}(0.625)\approx38.7^\circ$.
options.B:
(a) TIR occurs from air to glass because the ray bends towards the normal.
(b) $\sin i_c=1.6$, so $i_c=90^\circ$.
options.C:
(a) TIR cannot occur from air to glass because the angle of incidence is always zero.
(b) $\sin i_c=\dfrac{1.6}{1}=1.6$, so $i_c=53.1^\circ$.
options.D:
(a) TIR occurs from air to glass only when incidence exceeds the critical angle.
(b) $i_c=\sin^{-1}(1.6)\approx58^\circ$.
